instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Shred the Gruyère.
Trim a thin slice off the base of each endive. With the tip of a paring knife, cut a small cone out of the core, so the leaves stay together but the endive is less bitter.

Set a large lidded skillet over medium heat and melt 2 tbsp of the butter. Lay in the endives side by side, sprinkle with 1/2 tsp of the salt, and cook for 2 minutes per side, until they take on some golden color. If they don't all fit in one layer, brown them in two batches.
Add 1/3 cup of water to the skillet and cover. Cook over medium heat for 15 minutes, until the tip of a knife slides into the thickest part with no push.
Meanwhile, make the béchamel. Melt the remaining 3 tbsp butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the flour and stir for 1 minute. It should bubble and smell a little like toast, but stay pale.
Pour in the milk a splash at a time, whisking after each addition until it's smooth before you add more. Keep whisking over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes, until it coats the back of a spoon.
Take the pan off the heat. Stir in 1/2 cup of the Gruyère, the nutmeg, the remaining 1 tsp salt and the pepper. Taste the sauce and add a pinch more salt if it needs it.
Transfer the endives to a colander and press gently with the back of a spoon to push out the water. Pat them dry.
Wrap each endive in a slice of ham and lay them seam side down in a baking dish, close together.
Pour the béchamel over the top and sprinkle with the rest of the Gruyère.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until the top is bubbling and golden brown. For more color, turn on the broiler for the last 2 minutes and watch closely.
Let it sit for 5 minutes. Taste a little of the sauce. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve with slices of the baguette.
method_notes: The sources agree on the shape: endives cooked until tender, wrapped in ham, covered with béchamel and cheese and baked until golden. They differ on how the endives are cooked: the lead browns them in butter and braises them in a little water, while the others boil them for about 20 minutes. I followed the lead because browning adds flavor and the endives stay less watery, then pressed them dry before wrapping. Ratings are thin: the lead shows 5 from 1 vote on the page (JSON-LD not shown), and Jow shows 845 ratings with no average, so this is a fallback lead. I left out the honey in the lead and added nutmeg, which two of the other versions use.
